points.text: No test passes `--names-only`. I re-ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and got 10 tests OK, but none of them exercises the new option. The PR line "Verified: names-only" therefore claims something the suite doesn't check. Add CLI tests in `tests/test_cli.py` for three things the entry states: (1) with `--names-only` the output is one place name per line, (2) it has no distance and no count line, and (3) without the option the output is unchanged. Also, the history can't show a failing-test commit before the implementation, because no test exists. Commit the tests first so they fail, then the implementation, so the TDD order is visible.

The PR stamps the entry (`verified: by process:pilot-dev`, `pilot.verifiedCommit: 4f9e2ab`). A PR never stamps an entry, and only a `wiki lint` that finds the entry conforming writes the stamp. The stamp is also unsupported: the entry has no test and was never checked. Clear it with `python3 .pilot/pilot.py wiki set names-only --clear-stamp` so `verifiedAt` and `verifiedCommit` are empty. Keep `pilot.status: implemented` once the tests above exist and pass.

The PR adds no test that passes `--names-only`. The 10 passing tests were all there before, so the green run says nothing about the new behavior. TDD is not shown either: there is no failing-test commit before the implementation. Add tests in `tests/test_cli.py` that pass `--names-only`. They must check one name per line, no distance, no count line, and that the output without the option is unchanged. Commit the failing tests before the implementation, or otherwise make the test-first order visible in the history.

The wiki entry carries a stamp (`verified: by process:pilot-dev`, `pilot.verifiedCommit: 4f9e2ab`). A PR never stamps an entry, and only a `wiki lint` writes `verifiedAt`. Clear it with `wiki set --clear-stamp`. The stamp is also false, because nothing tested the behavior at that commit. Keep the status change to `implemented`, since this PR completes the entry.
The PR description says 'Verified: names-only ... OK (10 tests)', but no test exercises the option. Fix the description so it does not claim verification of this behavior.

The ordering of the `--names-only` output is not specified or tested. `search()` returns results farthest first today. If that order is kept, the new option inherits it without anyone having chosen it. Confirm in a test the order that the entry and the existing output imply, and do not change `search.py` for this.

The PR stamps the wiki entry (`verified: by process:pilot-dev`, `pilot.verifiedCommit: 4f9e2ab`). A PR never stamps an entry, and only a wiki lint writes the stamp. Remove the stamp and leave `verifiedAt` and `verifiedCommit` empty. The `implemented` status can stay if no other dev task listed on the entry is still open.

No test covers `--names-only`. `tests/test_cli.py` and `tests/test_search.py` never pass the option, and the PR adds none. The PR description says `Verified: names-only … OK (10 tests)`, but my re-run of `python -m unittest discover -s tests` gives the same 10 tests, all passing. Those tests exercise only the old behavior, so the claim is not backed. Add tests in `tests/test_cli.py` that check the entry's two rules: with the option, one name per line, with no distance and no count line; without it, the output is unchanged. Commit the failing tests before the implementation so the history shows red-green. As it stands, no failing-test commit exists, so TDD is not demonstrated.

No test exercises `--names-only`. I re-ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and got 10 tests OK, but `tests/test_cli.py` and `tests/test_search.py` never pass the option, and the PR adds none. They should cover: with `--names-only`, one name per line, no distance and no count line; without the option, the output is unchanged. Also cover the combination with a filter (step-free) so the option is checked against the real search path.

Also keep the order that the entry leaves open: names-only output must follow the existing search order, and the tests should state it, since `search()` returns farthest first today.
